text:
kevin: Heads-up — saw a p99 spike during 11:10 canary for requests routed EU->APAC fallback. throughput stable but tail doubled. attaching quick notes.

maria: ack. p50/p95 look fine, p99 subset doubled. seems correlated with cross-region fallbacks and batching tail.

oleg: do we have any kernel-selection changes around that time? I landed a small hint-priority tweak yesterday for long-context paths.

kevin: timeline matches your push @oleg. did a quick flamegraph, found an unexpected memcpy hotspot when fallback model lacked the quantized kernel layout.

raj: KV cache metrics show a tiny bump in local evictions during the same window — could cause remote KV fetches and longer seq processing.

natalie: can someone paste a sampled p99 trace? want to see queuing vs network vs kernel time.

kevin: sample trace below (single p99 request):
```
incoming -> route(EU->APAC fallback)
microbatch enqueue wait 34ms
kv-miss remote fetch 48ms
kernel-select layout-copy 14ms
kernel exec 19ms
serialize/stream 7ms
```

maria: that enqueue wait + remote KV trip is additive. when routing chooses APAC fallback we get RTT + remote cache miss + copy cost. tail multiplies.

oleg: the layout-copy is because we convert from int8-packed layout to native float buffers when compatible kernel isn't available on fallback. memcpy is ~14ms for 4-8k seq depending on buffer.

raj: short-term mitigation idea: prefer local degraded model variant for latency-critical traffic even if lower throughput/quality, and reduce batching wait for prioritized classes.

natalie: +1 on reducing max_wait for the priority SLO class. suggest 50ms -> 12ms. That will reduce batching amplification at tail.

kevin: ran offline replay: policy prefer-local + max_wait 12ms -> simulated p99 down ~38% on affected routes, throughput drop ~5% at peak.

maria: acceptable trade for SLO-critical paths. Need a rollout plan and guardrail so we don't regress global throughput too much.

oleg: mid-term: change kernel-hint table to include a "layout_compat_priority" so selection prefers compatible kernels (avoid copies) when routing indicates potential region fallback. Slight FLOPS loss but tail improves.

raj: also add per-route kv-hit metric into routing decision: if local kv-hit < 95% prefer local-model fallback to avoid remote fetch.

infra-bot: deploy-plan created: canary=10% -> 30% after 30m if p99 <= baseline*1.15. owner=kevin. ticket=INF-2189 :thumbsup:

kevin: I'll implement three steps: (1) routing guardrail to prefer local degraded variant for SLO-critical routes, (2) reduce max_wait for priority class to 12ms, (3) add layout_compat_priority to kernel-hints. Posting perf numbers after canary.

natalie: please include shorteval on a quality set for the degraded variant to ensure no unexpected regressions in outputs.

kevin: will do. also logging note: add a p99 trace sampler flag for buckle points (enqueue, kv-remote, layout-copy) so we can correlate quickly next time.

maria: thanks. once canary numbers in, we'll decide whether to widen or tune further.

oleg: long-term research item: look into on-the-fly kernel adapters to avoid full layout copies — smaller copy chunks or in-place remapping. could shave the 10-15ms.

raj: logging action: emit per-request flags when fallback chosen + kv-hit boolean + kernel-layout-used. will help root-cause.

infra-bot: note: canary scheduled at 12:00 UTC. monitoring alert rule INF-FALLBACK-P99 lowered for the window.

kevin: thanks team. starting implementation now.
